question: A man has to cover a distance of 168 km in 18 hours. If he covers two-thirds of this distance in (2)/(6) of the time, then what should be his speed (in km/hr, rounded off to one decimal place) to cover the remaining distance in the time left ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance = 168 km, total time = 18 hr

Covered distance = (2/3)×168 = 112 km

Time taken = (2/6)×18 = 6 hr

Remaining distance = 168 − 112 = 56 km

Remaining time = 18 − 6 = 12 hr

Required speed = 56 ÷ 12 = 4.67 ≈ 4.7 km/hr

**∴ Answer = 4.7 km/hr**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total distance = 168 km, Total time = 18 hr

**Formula used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Distance covered = (2/3) × 168 = 112 km

⇒ Time taken = (2/6) × 18 = 6 hr

⇒ Remaining distance = 168 − 112 = 56 km

⇒ Remaining time = 18 − 6 = 12 hr

⇒ Speed = 56 ÷ 12 = 4.67 ≈ 4.7 km/hr

**∴ The required speed is 4.7 km/hr.**
